ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are seeking to significantly expand their copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, after discovery proceedings allegedly revealed the AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted recordings. The move to add over 61,000 recordings substantially escalates the scope of the litigation.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement across 30,000 works. The filing significantly broadens the existing action against the AI audio platform.

ip_top_stories.title: MiniMax loses bid to dismiss Disney copyright lawsuit over AI system
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has rejected Chinese AI company MiniMax's attempt to dismiss a copyright infringement lawsuit brought by Disney and Warner Bros. The ruling allows the case to proceed, marking a significant development in litigation over AI systems allegedly trained on or generating content from copyrighted material.

ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors pursuing copyright claims over Meta's Llama AI model have taken the unusual step of suing Meta's AI scientists directly, in addition to the company itself. The move represents an escalation in litigation strategy in the ongoing dispute over the use of copyrighted books for AI training.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards will implement a new policy on AI-generated content after a nominated anthology was withdrawn amid controversy over undisclosed AI use. The episode has prompted the prestigious comics industry awards to formally address AI disclosure for future submissions.

ip_further_links.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_further_links.summary: An artist has filed suit against the US Copyright Office after it refused to register a photograph he enhanced using AI, raising questions about where the line falls between human authorship and AI-generated content.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal action over AI voice cloning is prompting broader debate about whether vocal identity can be protected under existing intellectual property law.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering new regulations to address AI systems that summarise news content without compensation to publishers, framing it as a 'free riding' problem.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis argues that accumulating copyright litigation and legal uncertainty around training data could significantly constrain generative AI investment and development.

ip_further_links.title: Australia: Creative industries fight push to change copyright laws
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry groups are pushing back against government moves to relax copyright rules that would benefit AI companies training on copyrighted content.

ip_further_links.title: How Italy's SIAE Is Shaping the Future of Copyright Protection Amid AI
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's collecting society SIAE is taking an active role in shaping copyright frameworks to protect creators' rights in the context of AI training and generation.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions - Center for European Policy Analysis
ip_further_links.summary: CEPA analysis argues that the EU's existing copyright framework is creating a competitive disadvantage for European AI development compared to jurisdictions with broader training data exemptions.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing? — The Scholarly Kitchen
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how AI-driven changes in research behaviour are challenging scholarly publishers to rethink their user models and content delivery.

ip_further_links.title: Indonesia Weighs AI Royalty Agency to Protect Creators' Rights
ip_further_links.summary: Indonesia is considering establishing a dedicated AI royalty agency as part of broader efforts to modernise its copyright framework and ensure creators are compensated when their work is used in AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Library Orgs Urge Big Five to Address Digital Pricing — Publishers Weekly [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Major library organisations have called on the five largest publishers to reconsider digital content pricing models that they argue are restricting library access.
